accepted.s: Special Category Status (SCS) was first introduced in India in 1969 on the recommendation of which body?
accepted.x: Special Category Status was introduced in 1969 on the recommendation of the Fifth Finance Commission. The National Development Council later endorsed the Gadgil Formula for Plan fund distribution.
accepted.tq: Identify the recommending body rather than the institution that later endorsed the related formula.
accepted.sec: SCS origin - year, recommending body, first states granted  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Gadgil Formula, under which Special Category States received preferential Central assistance, was endorsed by the National Development Council during:
accepted.x: The National Development Council endorsed the Gadgil Formula during 1968-69. The formula was used for distributing Plan funds, with preferential assistance for Special Category States.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the formula’s endorsement from the year in which SCS was introduced.
accepted.sec: SCS origin - year, recommending body, first states granted  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets correctly represents the first three States to be granted Special Category Status?
accepted.x: The first three States granted Special Category Status were Jammu & Kashmir, Assam and Nagaland.
accepted.tq: Start with the known first recipients and reject later additions to the category.
accepted.sec: SCS origin - year, recommending body, first states granted  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Special Category Status:
1. It is expressly provided for in the Constitution of India.
2. It was an executive and Planning Commission-era classification.
3. It was associated with preferential Central assistance under Plan fund distribution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Special Category Status is not a constitutional category; it emerged as an executive and Planning Commission-era classification linked to preferential Plan assistance.
accepted.tq: Test whether the classification is constitutional or executive before considering its financial consequence.
accepted.sec: SCS origin - year, recommending body, first states granted  [APPSC]

accepted.s: On which date did Prime Minister Manmohan Singh assure the Rajya Sabha that Andhra Pradesh would receive Special Category Status?
accepted.x: The assurance was given in the Rajya Sabha on 20 February 2014.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date to distinguish the parliamentary assurance from later Finance Commission developments.
accepted.sec: Rajya Sabha assurance on SCS for AP - date, who gave it, duration  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who gave the assurance in the Rajya Sabha regarding Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh in February 2014?
accepted.x: Prime Minister Manmohan Singh gave the assurance in the Rajya Sabha during the 2014 debates.
accepted.tq: Match the parliamentary assurance with the political office-holder who gave it.
accepted.sec: Rajya Sabha assurance on SCS for AP - date, who gave it, duration  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For how long was Special Category Status assured to Andhra Pradesh in the Rajya Sabha in 2014?
accepted.x: The assurance concerned Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh for five years.
accepted.tq: Test the exact duration rather than the date or the person associated with the assurance.
accepted.sec: Rajya Sabha assurance on SCS for AP - date, who gave it, duration  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a reason for the Centre later treating the assurance on Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh as non-binding?
o: It was rejected by the Fifth Finance Commission
It was not written into the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act
It was applicable only to Union Territories
It was withdrawn by the Rajya Sabha on the same day
accepted.x: The assurance was not incorporated into the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, enabling the Centre later to treat it as non-binding.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal consequence of an assurance not being incorporated into the governing statute.
accepted.sec: Rajya Sabha assurance on SCS for AP - date, who gave it, duration  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following States was included among those granted Special Category Status?
accepted.x: Uttarakhand was among the 11 States granted Special Category Status. Bihar, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh were states that sought but were never granted SCS.
accepted.tq: Separate the States that were granted SCS from States whose demands remained unfulfilled.
accepted.sec: SCS states - granted, never granted, pending demands  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following States:
1. Bihar
2. Odisha
3. Andhra Pradesh
4. Uttarakhand
Which of the above were never granted Special Category Status despite demands or claims for it?
accepted.x: Bihar, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh were never granted Special Category Status. Uttarakhand was among the States that received it.
accepted.tq: Classify each State before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: SCS states - granted, never granted, pending demands  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the 11 States listed as having been granted Special Category Status?
accepted.x: Telangana has never been granted Special Category Status. Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Tripura are included among the 11 SCS States.
accepted.tq: Find the State wrongly inserted into an otherwise genuine list of SCS recipients.
accepted.sec: SCS states - granted, never granted, pending demands  [other exams]

accepted.s: Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory in:
accepted.x: Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory in 2019. It had earlier been one of the first States granted Special Category Status.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the later constitutional-status change from the earlier grant of SCS.
accepted.sec: SCS states - granted, never granted, pending demands  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Centre was apprehensive that granting Special Category Status to Andhra Pradesh would lead to similar demands from:
accepted.x: The Centre feared that granting SCS to Andhra Pradesh would trigger identical demands from Bihar and Odisha.
accepted.tq: Link the policy decision with the States whose similar claims created political concern.
accepted.sec: SCS states - granted, never granted, pending demands  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a parameter associated with eligibility for Special Category Status under the Gadgil-Mukherjee framework?
o: High population density and high urbanisation
accepted.x: High population density and high urbanisation are not listed as eligibility parameters. The criteria included difficult terrain, low population density or a sizeable tribal population, strategic location, backwardness and non-viable finances.
accepted.tq: Locate the reversed population criterion among the genuine eligibility features.
accepted.sec: SCS criteria - Gadgil-Mukherjee formula parameters, eligibility features

accepted.s:
Consider the following features:
1. Hilly and difficult terrain
2. Low population density or sizeable tribal population
3. Strategic location along international borders
4. Economic and infrastructural backwardness
5. Non-viable State finances
Which of the above were weighed while considering Special Category Status?
accepted.x: All five listed features were considered under the SCS criteria. The broad rationale combined geographical disadvantage with economic and infrastructural backwardness.
accepted.tq: Check each criterion against the complete eligibility framework before using the all-inclusive option.
accepted.sec: SCS criteria - Gadgil-Mukherjee formula parameters, eligibility features

accepted.s: Which formula was introduced in 1991 as the later version of the Gadgil Formula for Plan transfers to States?
accepted.x: The Gadgil Formula was later modified and became the Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula in 1991.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original formula from its later modified version by the year of modification.
accepted.sec: SCS criteria - Gadgil-Mukherjee formula parameters, eligibility features

accepted.s: Under the Plan transfer arrangement associated with the Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula, Special Category States received:
o: No Central assistance until their finances became viable
A reserved first share of Normal Central Assistance
A share exclusively from State taxes
accepted.x: Special Category States received a reserved first share of Normal Central Assistance under the Plan transfer arrangement.
accepted.tq: Test the precise financial preference rather than the broader idea of Central assistance.
accepted.sec: SCS criteria - Gadgil-Mukherjee formula parameters, eligibility features

accepted.s: Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme funding pattern, the Centre-State ratio for a Special Category State was:
accepted.x: For Special Category States, Centrally Sponsored Schemes followed a 90:10 Centre-State funding ratio. The corresponding ratio for general States was 60:40.
accepted.tq: Compare the funding ratios directly and watch for reversal of Centre and State shares.
accepted.sec: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares Centrally Sponsored Scheme funding for Special Category and general States?
accepted.x: The Centre-State ratio was 90:10 for Special Category States and 60:40 for general States.
accepted.tq: Use the paired comparison to avoid reversing the two categories or the order of contributions.
accepted.sec: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a benefit available to Special Category States in respect of Central loans?
o: Interest fixed at the normal market rate only
Complete waiver of every Central loan
Loans available only through private banks
accepted.x: Special Category States received Central loans at concessional interest rates, unlike the normal terms applicable to general States.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific concession without extending it into an unsupported loan waiver.
accepted.sec: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

accepted.s: Which of the following was associated with industries in Special Category States?
o: Tax breaks and incentives such as income-tax or excise-related concessions
Exemption only from State legislative taxes
accepted.x: Industrial units in Special Category States could receive tax breaks and incentives, including income-tax or excise-related concessions.
accepted.tq: Match the sector-specific SCS benefit with the correct type of fiscal incentive.
accepted.sec: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

accepted.s: What was the treatment of unspent funds in a Special Category State?
o: They lapsed at the end of the financial year
They did not lapse and could be carried forward
They were converted into Central loans
They were transferred automatically to general States
accepted.x: Unspent funds in Special Category States did not lapse and could be carried forward. In general States, such funds lapsed.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between lapse and carry-forward treatment.
accepted.sec: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

accepted.s: The Consumer Welfare Fund seed-money ratio mentioned for Special Category States, compared with general States, was:
accepted.x: The Consumer Welfare Fund seed-money ratio was 90:10 for Special Category States and 75:25 for general States.
accepted.tq: Read the paired numerical figures in the correct category order.
accepted.sec: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

accepted.s: Under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana criterion mentioned for Special Category States, habitations with a population of at least how many were covered?
accepted.x: PMGSY covered habitations of 250 or more in Special Category States, while the corresponding threshold in plains was 500 or more.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the lower SCS population threshold from the plains threshold.
accepted.sec: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the GST exemption threshold referred to for Special Category States?
o: It was abolished for Special Category States
It was the same as the threshold for all general States
accepted.x: The GST exemption threshold referred to for Special Category States was lower, at ₹10 lakh.
accepted.tq: Identify the direction of the comparison before selecting the exact figure.
accepted.sec: Benefits of SCS - central funding ratio, tax concessions, unspent funds

accepted.s: Who chaired the Fourteenth Finance Commission, whose award covered the period 2015-20?
accepted.x: Y.V. Reddy chaired the Fourteenth Finance Commission, whose award covered 2015-20.
accepted.tq: Match the Finance Commission number and award period with its chairperson.
accepted.sec: 14th Finance Commission position on SCS - what changed in devolution

accepted.s: The recommendation increasing the States’ share in the divisible pool to 42 per cent was accepted on:
accepted.x: The recommendation of the Fourteenth Finance Commission was accepted on 24 February 2015.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of acceptance from the award period and the later Sixteenth Finance Commission period.
accepted.sec: 14th Finance Commission position on SCS - what changed in devolution

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Fourteenth Finance Commission’s position concerning general and Special Category States?
o: It abolished all Central assistance to general States
It maintained a separate devolution formula exclusively for SCS States
It made no distinction between general and Special Category States
It reduced the States’ share of the divisible pool to 32 per cent
accepted.x: The Fourteenth Finance Commission made no distinction between general and Special Category States in the higher tax devolution arrangement. The Centre argued that the increased devolution subsumed SCS benefits.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversal of the Commission’s uniform treatment and the direction of devolution change.
accepted.sec: 14th Finance Commission position on SCS - what changed in devolution

accepted.s: The Fourteenth Finance Commission’s increase in the States’ share of the divisible pool to 42 per cent was described as:
o: A temporary increase applicable only to SCS States
The first reduction in tax devolution
accepted.x: The increase from 32 per cent to 42 per cent was described as the largest increase ever in the States’ share of the divisible pool.
accepted.tq: Reject options that reverse the scale, direction or applicability of the devolution change.
accepted.sec: 14th Finance Commission position on SCS - what changed in devolution

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Fourteenth Finance Commission — 42 per cent
2. Fifteenth Finance Commission — 41 per cent
3. Sixteenth Finance Commission — 41 per cent and a Contribution to GDP criterion
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended 42 per cent, while the Fifteenth and Sixteenth Finance Commissions retained 41 per cent; the Sixteenth also added a 10 per cent Contribution to GDP criterion.
accepted.tq: Track the changing devolution percentages across successive Finance Commissions.
accepted.sec: 14th Finance Commission position on SCS - what changed in devolution

accepted.s: Under the Sixteenth Finance Commission arrangement mentioned, the weight assigned to the ‘Contribution to GDP’ criterion was:
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission added Contribution to GDP as a criterion with a 10 per cent weight.
accepted.tq: Focus on the exact weight assigned to the newly added criterion.
accepted.sec: 14th Finance Commission position on SCS - what changed in devolution

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Special Assistance Package was offered to Andhra Pradesh
B. Prime Minister gave the Rajya Sabha assurance on SCS for five years
C. Fourteenth Finance Commission award was used to deny SCS
D. TDP broke from the NDA
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 2014 assurance, 2015 Fourteenth Finance Commission award, September 2016 Special Assistance Package, and 2018 withdrawal of TDP from the NDA.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest event first and then place the 2015 and 2016 financial-policy developments before the 2018 political event.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: In September 2016, the Centre offered Andhra Pradesh:
o: A separate constitutional amendment granting SCS
A higher share of 50 per cent in the divisible pool
A Special Assistance Package instead of Special Category Status
A complete waiver of all State debts
accepted.x: In September 2016, a Special Assistance Package was offered to Andhra Pradesh instead of granting Special Category Status.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the alternative package from the status that Andhra Pradesh had demanded.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: Which political development took place in 2018 in the context of Andhra Pradesh’s Special Category Status demand?
o: TDP broke from the NDA and moved a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha
YSRCP joined the NDA and withdrew the demand
The Rajya Sabha enacted SCS through a constitutional amendment
The Centre granted SCS to Andhra Pradesh for ten years
accepted.x: In 2018, the TDP broke from the NDA and moved a no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha in July; the motion was defeated.
accepted.tq: Match the year with both linked political actions and avoid replacing a motion with a constitutional amendment.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: The TDP’s no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha related to the Andhra Pradesh SCS controversy was moved in:
accepted.x: The TDP moved the no-confidence motion in the Lok Sabha in July 2018, and the motion was defeated.
accepted.tq: Use the month and year to distinguish the parliamentary motion from the 2014 assurance and 2016 package.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: In 2019, the Special Category Status agitation in Andhra Pradesh was described as an:
accepted.x: The agitation became an ‘emotional referendum’ in 2019. The YSRCP campaign described the Special Assistance Package as a ‘betrayal’.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact political characterisation rather than a formal constitutional or administrative term.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: Which political party’s campaign branded the Special Assistance Package as a ‘betrayal’ during the 2019 agitation?
accepted.x: The YSRCP campaign branded the Special Assistance Package a ‘betrayal’ during the 2019 SCS agitation.
accepted.tq: Match the political slogan with the party associated with it.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the revival of the Andhra Pradesh Special Category Status demand in 2026?
o: It was raised only by the Finance Commission and not in Parliament
It was raised by Manickam Tagore in the Lok Sabha, Botcha Satyanarayana and Y.S. Sharmila
It was raised exclusively by the Union Finance Ministry
It was withdrawn by all Andhra Pradesh political parties
accepted.x: The demand was revived in 2026 through interventions by Congress MP Manickam Tagore in the Lok Sabha, YSRCP leader Botcha Satyanarayana and APCC chief Y.S. Sharmila.
accepted.tq: Group the individuals with the correct year and political context instead of attributing the demand to an institution.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: Manickam Tagore raised the Special Category Status issue in the Lok Sabha during debate on the:
accepted.x: Manickam Tagore raised the demand during debate on the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill in 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the parliamentary intervention with the specific Bill under debate.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: Which of the following best states Andhra Pradesh’s argument regarding the 2014 parliamentary assurance?
o: Only a Finance Commission recommendation can create a constitutional obligation
A commitment made on the floor of Parliament carries constitutional weight
A parliamentary assurance automatically expires when a State is bifurcated
The assurance applied only to the successor State of Telangana
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh argued that a commitment made on the floor of Parliament carries constitutional weight, even though the assurance was not written into the Reorganisation Act.
accepted.tq: Apply the political-constitutional argument to the status of a parliamentary commitment.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions

accepted.s: Why did Andhra Pradesh argue that the 42 per cent devolution recommended by the Fourteenth Finance Commission did not resolve its SCS-related concerns?
o: It applied to all States and did not address Andhra Pradesh’s asymmetric loss of Hyderabad
It replaced the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act entirely
It was available only to States with international borders
The 42 per cent devolution applied only to Andhra Pradesh and excluded all other States
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh argued that the 42 per cent devolution applied uniformly to all States and therefore did not compensate for its asymmetric loss of Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Test whether a general fiscal measure addressed the State-specific consequence of bifurcation.
accepted.sec: AP SCS controversy - political events, protests, Parliament motions
